events.title: February Revolution Begins in Petrograd
events.description: On March 8, 1917 (February 23 in the Julian calendar then used in Russia), International Women's Day demonstrations by women textile workers in Petrograd grew into mass strikes and protests against food shortages and the war. Within days, the unrest spread among workers and soldiers.
events.significance: The protests escalated into the February Revolution, which forced Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate and ended the Romanov dynasty's three-century rule, paving the way for the Bolshevik takeover later that year.

events.title: U.S. Supreme Court Rules on Religious Instruction in Public Schools
events.description: In McCollum v. Board of Education, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled 8-1 that a program allowing religious instruction in public school classrooms in Champaign, Illinois violated the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment.
events.significance: The decision strengthened the principle of separation of church and state in American public education and shaped later rulings on religion in schools.

events.title: First U.S. Combat Troops Land in South Vietnam
events.description: About 3,500 U.S. Marines came ashore at Da Nang, South Vietnam, becoming the first American combat troops deployed in the country, ostensibly to protect the nearby air base.
events.significance: The landing marked a major escalation of U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War, which grew to hundreds of thousands of troops and became one of the most divisive conflicts in American history.

events.title: Philips Demonstrates the Compact Disc Prototype
events.description: Philips publicly demonstrated its prototype digital audio compact disc to the press in Eindhoven, Netherlands, showcasing optical disc technology for music playback. Philips later partnered with Sony to set the CD standard.
events.significance: The demonstration was a key step toward the commercial launch of the CD in 1982, which transformed the music industry and popularized digital media storage.

events.title: Disappearance of Malaysia Airlines Flight 370
events.description: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, a Boeing 777 carrying 239 people from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing, vanished from radar shortly after takeoff. Investigators concluded it diverted from its route and likely ended in the southern Indian Ocean.
events.significance: It became one of the greatest mysteries in aviation history, prompting the largest and most expensive search in aviation history and leading to reforms in aircraft tracking requirements.
